jurisdiction.name: Cyprus
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Cyprus is replacing its 2020 national AI strategy with a draft AI Strategy 2032 and is implementing the EU AI Act through a draft AI Law; both went to public consultation in summer 2026. In January 2025 the Council of Ministers designated the Commissioner of Communications as notifying authority, lead market surveillance authority and single point of contact, with the Data Protection Commissioner supervising certain high-risk uses. A 2026 amendment to the copyright law creates a right against deepfakes, and the Ministry of Education issued an AI policy for schools in 2025.
lead_institutions: Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy
Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft AI strategy and AI law are recorded as consultation drafts, and one cabinet decision could only be located because its published copy is a scan.

instruments.summary: Cyprus's first national AI strategy (version 1.6), drafted by the Department of Electronic Communications with a group of AI experts and aligned with the EU Coordinated Plan on AI. It sets actions under four pillars: maximising investment through partnerships (business, public sector, research, standardisation, an AI centre of excellence, digital innovation hub), national data spaces (open and research data portals), talent and lifelong learning, and ethical and trustworthy AI, including a proposed National Committee on Ethical and Trustworthy AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: The national AI strategy currently on the official record; a replacement National AI Strategy 2032 was in public consultation until 31 August 2026.

instruments.summary: Draft national AI strategy prepared by the National AI Taskforce, chaired by the Chief Scientist for Research, Innovation and Technology, with the vision that by 2032 Cyprus is recognised as the trusted AI hub in the Eastern Mediterranean. It sets eight national strategic objectives (trusted AI jurisdiction, productivity, ecosystem, AI-enabled public services, skills, secure and sovereign data and infrastructure, governance, ethics and accountability, sovereign capabilities), priority sectors, and governance enablers including an AI use-case lifecycle with control gates and AI Officer roles in government.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Proposed successor to the 2020 national AI strategy; sets the planned national AI governance and public-sector adoption model.

instruments.summary: Announces the Council of Ministers decision of 22 January 2025 designating Cyprus's national competent authorities under Article 70 of the EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689). The Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy coordinates national implementation and represents Cyprus on the AI Board; the Commissioner of Communications is notifying authority, market surveillance authority and single point of contact; the Commissioner for Personal Data Protection is market surveillance authority for Annex III points 1, 6, 7 and 8 high-risk systems and supervises Article 5 prohibited practices within her remit.

instruments.issuing_authority: Commissioner of Communications (Office of the Commissioner of Electronic Communications and Postal Regulation)
instruments.current_status: Consultation draft posted by the Commissioner of Communications on the government e-consultation platform on 16 August 2026 and open for comments until 16 September 2026 (status shown as under processing); it is marked TLP AMBER and was not found as a bill before the House of Representatives or in the Official Gazette as of 12 October 2026. It would enter into force on publication in the Official Gazette.
instruments.summary: Draft national law implementing the EU AI Act. It designates the Commissioner of Communications (acting through a new AI Regulation Directorate) as notifying authority, market surveillance authority and single point of contact, the Commissioner for Personal Data Protection as market surveillance authority for Annex III point 1 (law enforcement, border and justice uses) and points 6-8, and the Central Bank of Cyprus for high-risk AI used by financial institutions it supervises. It sets investigation, information and sanctioning powers with administrative fines, a power to authorise real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement under Article 5 conditions, and a national AI regulatory sandbox run by the Commissioner with the Data Protection Commissioner.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Proposed national AI Act implementing law: authorities, enforcement, fines and the AI regulatory sandbox.

instruments.english_title: First Milestone for the Implementation of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence in Cyprus (list of Article 77 fundamental-rights authorities)
instruments.issuing_authority: Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy
instruments.current_status: List notified to the European Commission and announced on 6 November 2024; the Article 77 powers apply from 2 August 2026. The list is to be revised when necessary.
instruments.summary: Announces the list of three national public authorities notified to the European Commission under Article 77 of the EU AI Act as bodies that supervise or enforce Union fundamental-rights law in relation to high-risk AI: the Commissioner for Personal Data Protection, the Commissioner for Administration and the Protection of Human Rights (Ombudsman) and the Attorney General of the Republic. These bodies gain additional powers under the AI Act from 2 August 2026, and the list is to be reviewed as needed.

instruments.english_title: Law on the Protection of Natural Persons with regard to the Processing of Personal Data and the Free Movement of such Data of 2018 (Law 125(I)/2018)
instruments.issuing_authority: House of Representatives (published by the Commissioner for Personal Data Protection)
instruments.current_status: Published in the Official Gazette on 31 July 2018 (No. 4670) and in force; amended by Law 26(I)/2022. The Commissioner publishes an unofficial English translation. The law has no commencement clause stating a separate effective date.
instruments.summary: Cyprus's national law implementing the GDPR, which governs the processing of personal data used to train and run AI systems. It sets national choices such as 14 as the age of digital consent for information-society services, a ban on processing genetic and biometric data for health and life insurance, conditions for processing such data requiring an impact assessment and prior consultation with the Commissioner, and the powers and fines of the Commissioner for Personal Data Protection; it repealed the 2001-2012 data protection laws.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Data protection law that applies to AI processing of personal data; the Commissioner it empowers is also an AI Act authority.

instruments.official_title: Ο περί του Δικαιώματος Πνευματικής Ιδιοκτησίας και Συγγενικών Δικαιωμάτων (Τροποποιητικός) Νόμος του 2026 (Ν. 29(Ι)/2026)
instruments.english_title: Copyright and Related Rights (Amendment) Law of 2026 (Law 29(I)/2026) on deepfakes
instruments.current_status: Published in the Official Gazette No. 5080 (Annex I, Part I) on 23 March 2026 and in force; the law states no separate commencement date. It amends the Copyright and Related Rights Laws 1976 to 2022.
instruments.summary: Amends the Copyright and Related Rights Law 59/1976 to create a sui generis right against AI deepfakes, citing the rapid development of AI. It defines 'deepfake product' by reference to Article 3(60) of the EU AI Act and 'personal physical characteristics' (including voice and biometric data), and prohibits making available to the public, without explicit consent, deepfake imitations of a performer's performance (new article 49) or of a natural person's physical characteristics (new article 50), with exceptions for caricature, satire, parody and political or social critique unless the imitation is disinformation posing a serious risk. Protection lasts 50 years after death; copyright civil remedies apply, and breach of article 50 is added to the offences in article 14.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First Cypriot law with AI-specific provisions: consent-based protection and a criminal offence against unauthorised deepfakes.

instruments.english_title: Policy and Guidelines for the Responsible and Ethical Use of Artificial Intelligence in Primary and Secondary Education
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth (Cyprus Pedagogical Institute)
instruments.current_status: Presented by the Minister of Education on 16 October 2025 and sent to all public and private schools by circular of 26 November 2025. The circular names https://www.pi.ac.cy/aipolicy2025 as the direct link, which returned a not-found page on 12 October 2026; the full text is on the Ministry school network (sch.cy). A follow-up action plan is announced.
instruments.summary: Ministry of Education policy text and guidelines for the use of AI in primary and secondary schools, addressed to teachers, pupils, parents and carers, prepared by the Ministry's AI working group with an advisory committee of international and Cypriot experts. It sets principles (human-centred approach, AI literacy and critical thinking, pedagogical use, ethics, compliance and protection) and guidance on age limits for AI and generative-AI tools (including under-13 restrictions and parental consent), terms of use, personal data and privacy, bias, data validity and ethical content creation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sector policy for AI use in schools, implementing the Ministry's AI-in-education roadmap.
